titulo: To believe or not to believe
intro: Religions and beliefs, the Catholic vocabulary that fills Spanish life and language, and a few words of philosophy.
p.el alma.nota: Feminine, but el alma in the singular, like el agua.
b1.texto:
**Religions.** **El cristianismo** (**el catolicismo**, **el protestantismo**), **el islam**, **el judaísmo**, **el budismo**, **el hinduismo**. The adjectives are not written with a capital: **católico**, **musulmán**, **judío**, **budista**.

**Positions.** **Ser creyente**, **practicante** or **no practicante**, **ateo**, **agnóstico**. **Tener fe.** **Convertirse al** budismo. **Un Estado laico** has no official religion.

**Catholic vocabulary.** It is everywhere in Spain, even among non-believers. **La iglesia** (the building) and **la Iglesia** (the institution). **El cura** or **el sacerdote**, **el obispo**, **el papa**, **la monja**, **el monje**. **La misa**, **el bautizo**, **la comunión**, **la confesión**. **Rezar** una **oración**. **El pecado**, **el cielo**, **el infierno**, **el alma**, **el milagro**.

**The calendar.** **La Navidad**, **los Reyes Magos** (6 January, when Spanish children get their presents), **la Semana Santa** with its **procesiones**, **el santo** of each person.

**Religion in the language.** Dozens of everyday phrases keep it alive: **¡Dios mío!** **Gracias a Dios.** **Si Dios quiere.** **Ojalá** (from Arabic: may God will it). **Adiós** (to God). **Ser un santo** (to be very patient). **Hacer un milagro** (to manage the impossible). **Llegar y besar el santo** (to succeed at the first attempt).

**Philosophy.** **La razón** and **la fe**. **El pensamiento**, **el conocimiento**, **la ética**. **Razonar**, **reflexionar sobre**, **plantearse** una pregunta. **El sentido de la vida.** **El más allá.**

**Oración** has two meanings: a prayer and, in grammar, a sentence.
b2.f0: Spain has, according to its Constitution, no official religion, and fewer and fewer Spaniards say they are practising believers.
b2.f1: However, during Holy Week the streets of hundreds of cities fill with processions.
b2.f2: Thousands of people carry for hours images that weigh tons, many of them without having set foot in a church all year.
b2.f3: Some do it out of faith, others because of a promise, and quite a few because their father and grandfather did it.
b2.f4: There are convinced atheists who weep as the Virgin of their neighbourhood goes by.
b2.f5: Whoever wants to understand it should not ask about religion but about belonging.
b2.f6: For many, the procession is not so much a prayer as a way of saying where they are from.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why do many non-believers take part in the processions?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Porque lo hicieron su padre y su abuelo.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Being paid is a distractor; the question asks about tradition and belonging.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what is a procession for many people?
b5.o0.refuerzo: La manera de decir de dónde son.
b5.o2.refuerzo: A tourist show is a distractor; the question asks what a procession means to people.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Un Estado laico is a state with no official religion: laico means secular.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Laico has nothing to do with lazy.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Feminine nouns beginning with stressed a take el in the singular.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Before stressed a, the singular article is el.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Lo is neuter and never goes with a noun.
b8.pregunta: In a grammar book, una oración is…
b9.o0: He passed first time: instant success.
b9.o1: He passed first: he arrived and kissed the saint.
b9.o1.explicacion: The idiom means succeeding at the first attempt.
b9.o2: He passed thanks to a miracle.
b9.o2.explicacion: The idiom is about succeeding at once.
b10.traduccion: Fewer and fewer Spaniards say they are practising believers.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an essay on the place of religious traditions in a society where fewer and fewer people believe.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud a religious or traditional festival of your country to someone who knows nothing about it.
b9.o0.explicacion: Aprobó a la primera means he passed on the first attempt, with no miracle involved.
